eyebrow: Git & GitHub for Software Engineers · Chapter 3, Lesson 14
subtitle: Finding the commit, author, and reasoning behind any line

code:
$ git blame src/pricing.py
a3f91c2e (Priya Shah 2025-11-02) def apply_discount(price, pct):
a3f91c2e (Priya Shah 2025-11-02)     # capped at 40%, JIRA-2291
f7c1a0b8 (Dan Okafor 2026-02-18)     pct = min(pct, 0.40)
caption: "Blame" is a misleading name — it's the fastest path to the reasoning, not a fault-finder.

code:
$ git show a3f91c2e
Author: Priya Shah
Date:   Sun Nov 2 2025

    Cap discount at 40% per legal review (JIRA-2291)

    Legal flagged uncapped discounts as a contract risk...
caption: blame finds the commit. The commit message is what actually answers "why."

eyebrow: Finding when code appeared — or vanished
code:
$ git log -S "MAX_RETRIES" --oneline
e4c8a91 Lower retry ceiling after incident review
b2f0d73 Add exponential backoff with configurable retry limit
caption: The pickaxe searches every diff — including commits that deleted the line blame can't show you.
